props.title: What Does the Lymphatic System Actually Do?
props.text: Your lymphatic system is a network of vessels and lymph nodes. It moves excess fluid out of your tissues and carries immune cells and waste around the body. It has no pump of its own, so it depends on breathing, movement and muscle activity. When you sit still for hours, like on a long flight, fluid can build up and your legs or ankles can feel heavy or puffy. Lymphatic drainage massage uses slow, light strokes to encourage that flow, and it can leave you feeling lighter. It is a relaxation treatment, not a medical one.

items.question: How long is a lymphatic massage, and which length should I choose?
items.answer: Sessions run 1, 1.5 or 2 hours. One hour suits a first session or mild heaviness after travel. The longer sessions give more time across the whole body.

items.question: Where can I get lymphatic drainage massage in Seminyak?

items.question: Is Lymphatic Massage the same as Deep Tissue Massage?
items.answer: No. Deep tissue massage uses firm pressure on deeper muscle layers. Lymphatic massage at Spa Bali Moon uses very light, rhythmic strokes that follow the lymph pathways just under the skin.

items.question: Can Lymphatic Massage help with swollen legs after travelling?
items.answer: It's often chosen for that. Long flights, road trips and long periods of sitting can cause temporary fluid retention, and gentle lymphatic drainage can leave your legs feeling lighter and more comfortable. If your legs are painful, red or swollen on one side only, see a doctor first.

items.question: Does Lymphatic Massage remove toxins from the body?
items.answer: Your lymphatic system already carries waste and excess fluid away. Lymphatic massage supports that normal process, but it is not a medical detox treatment.

items.question: Will the massage feel gentle?
items.answer: Yes. The pressure is deliberately light because lymph vessels sit close to the skin. Firm pressure isn't needed.

items.question: Can I combine Lymphatic Massage with other spa treatments?
items.answer: Yes. Many guests add a facial, foot reflexology or a body treatment to the same visit. Tell us when you book.

items.question: Is lymphatic drainage real?
items.answer: Lymphatic drainage is a real massage technique: a gentle method designed to encourage the movement of lymph fluid. It's commonly used to help with swelling and relaxation, but it is not a cure for any medical condition.

items.question: Does lymphatic drainage work on the face?
items.answer: Facial lymphatic drainage uses gentle movements around the face and neck to encourage lymph flow. It can help reduce temporary puffiness and leave the face feeling refreshed.

items.question: Can lymphatic drainage make you sick?
items.answer: It's gentle, but some people feel tired, thirsty or slightly light-headed afterwards. Drink water and rest. If you feel unwell or have a medical condition, check with a doctor before booking.
